hero.claim: I build custom websites, online stores and platforms.
hero.subclaim: For companies with a clear idea and nobody to build it.

pact.title: What happens if you write to me
pact.intro: I'm Andrea. I've been building software for the web for six years, both inside companies and on my own projects. On small projects I work alone, on large ones in a team — and either way the part I care about is the same: understanding the problem before writing code.

reply.title: I reply within 24 hours
reply.body: Always. Even if it's only to say your project isn't right for me, and who could help you instead.

call.title: Free 30-minute call
call.body: You tell me what you need, I tell you what I actually think. No sales pitch.

proposal.title: A written proposal
proposal.body: What I'll do, how long it takes, on what terms. In writing, not just spoken.

decide.title: You decide, unhurried
decide.body: If it doesn't convince you, we've lost half an hour. No commitment, no chasing.

services.title: What I build
services.intro: Four ways to work together. If your case sits between two of them, that's normal — we'll sort it out on the call.

sites.title: Custom sites and landing pages
sites.description: Your site is the first thing people see of you. I build it fast, findable on Google and genuinely yours — not a bought theme filled with text.

ecommerce.title: Online stores
ecommerce.description: Selling online without fighting your back office every day. Catalogue, payments, shipping and integration with the tools you already use.

webapp.title: Web apps and platforms
webapp.description: Custom back offices, portals and dashboards. For when the spreadsheet isn't enough any more and off-the-shelf software doesn't do what you need.

ai.title: AI and automation
ai.description: Assistants that actually answer, and automation that takes repetitive work off people. Not magic: tools wired to your real data.

works.title: Four problems, and how I solved them
works.intro: No logos and slogans here. You'll find the problem that existed, the decision I made, and why I rejected the easy alternative.

bdroppy.name: BDroppy
bdroppy.symptom: The platform was stuck on React 14. Every new feature took weeks and the team was afraid to touch the code.
bdroppy.decision: Rewriting from scratch was the comfortable choice, but the platform had to stay online and keep selling. I chose an incremental migration, route by route, with old and new running side by side.
bdroppy.outcome: A B2B dropshipping platform now on Next.js and TypeScript, migrated without ever taking the service down.

aidify.name: Aidify
aidify.symptom: A customer support team buried under the same ten questions, repeated across five different e-commerce platforms.
aidify.decision: Not a chatbot that guesses, but one wired to the real catalogue and real orders. And above all: when it doesn't know, it hands over to a person instead of inventing an answer.
aidify.outcome: An AI-based assistant integrated across several stores, absorbing the repetitive requests and leaving the real ones to people.

customertrack.name: CustomerTrack
customertrack.symptom: Physical shops that knew nothing about their own customers: how many came in, where they stopped, what they actually looked at.
customertrack.decision: Instead of a single product, a white-label solution: each chain uses it as if it were their own. It costs more to build and pays for itself from the second customer onwards.
customertrack.outcome: An in-store behaviour analytics platform, resellable to different brands without rewriting anything.

visualboost.name: VisualBoost
visualboost.symptom: An editorial image library nobody could browse without sitting there waiting.
visualboost.decision: The bottleneck was the images, not the code. Before anything else: modern formats, right dimensions and progressive loading.
visualboost.outcome: An image platform for fashion, food and beauty that stays fast even on large catalogues.

understand.title: We understand
understand.body: Before talking technology, I work out what has to happen in your business for the project to have been worth anything.

design.title: I design
design.body: Structure, screens and technical choices. We make the important decisions together — you don't discover them once the work is done.

build.title: I build
build.body: I work in deliverable pieces: you see something working early and often, not only at the end.

stay.title: I stay
stay.body: I don't disappear after launch. Fixes, changes and a person who answers: it's why clients come back.

idt.body: Complex features on an application used daily, and a shared component library that made the interface consistent across the product.

eroi.body: A B2B e-commerce platform end to end: frontend, APIs, database and the dashboard they run it from every day.

freelance.body: Complete projects for small and medium businesses, from gathering requirements to release. This is where I learned to talk to people who aren't technical.

client.title: I have a project
client.body: Tell me what you need. I reply within 24 hours, even when the answer is no.
